Subject: Realtime API - large requests producing long tails / partial chunks

Karthik / Redwood team,

We're seeing a growing number of requests in our realtime pipeline that return a flurry of partial chunk frames, then stall for ~8-12s, then burst the rest of the tokens. The client observes this as extreme latency spikes and occasional 502s when the client-side timeout fires. It started showing up after we moved a subset of traffic to the larger context model last week.

I captured session logs and a small repro; attaching the bundle. This is actively impacting our demo environment and we've had two demos slip today. Can someone confirm if this matches any known fragmentation/ordering regressions in your runtime?

Thanks,
Elena Morales
CTO, ClearSight AI

Attachments: p50-logs.tar.gz (12MB), repro_steps.txt
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@clearsight.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-05T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime API - large requests producing long tails / partial chunks

Elena — thanks for the report and for the logs. Short answer: we see a correlated increase in chunk reordering and stall gaps starting 2026-09-04 22:00 UTC for the ClearSight tenant. I'm looping engineering and CS.

Next steps from my side: 1) Neha to triage logs and confirm root cause signal; 2) Vanessa to assemble a mitigation plan (rollback/route policy); 3) I can coordinate an executive update if you want an SLA remediation conversation.

We will prioritize a hotfix if this matches our recent chunk coalescing change. We'll follow up with a timeline in the next 90 minutes.

—Karthik

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Realtime API - large requests producing long tails / partial chunks

On 2026-09-05 09:02, Karthik Iyer wrote:
> We will prioritize a hotfix if this matches our recent chunk coalescing change.

I pulled Elena's bundle and a matching runtime trace. Initial findings: there is a combination of 1) partial-chunk emission from the model worker and 2) proxy-level reordering during high-concurrent KV fetches. The worker emits a small leading frame, then stalls waiting on an async cache fill; the proxy queues additional frames and then flushes after a timeout, which looks like the burst Elena described.

Impact: we measured an increase in 95th/99th percentile per-request latency for ClearSight, and a 1.6% uptick in client-facing error-rate (timeouts and aborted connections) for their trial cluster. This correlates exactly with the coalescing optimization we shipped 2026-09-03.

Repro: reproduce in staging with the attached repro_steps.txt in ~10 iterations.

I'll start a code rollback candidate now and test on canary. Grace, please advise if we should open an exec incident given the customer impact and demo slippage.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

-Vanessa

Karthik / Grace / team,

Thanks for the rapid attention. We were routed off the problematic coalescing path last night and the burstiness is gone in our demo cluster. Latency p95 dropped ~420ms and timeout errors are down to baseline. The team accepted the 10% credit offer and appreciated the proactive comms.

A couple of asks as we move toward GA next quarter: 1) a formal postmortem that covers why the coalescing optimization regressed under concurrent KV conditions, 2) a plan for guardrails on shipping runtime batching optimizations (feature flag gating + canary heuristics), and 3) a contact for escalation path if we hit similar regressions during large-customer demos.

Happy to join a postmortem review.

—Elena
